To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complex interplay in which teacher-related variables influence ICT integration in the Chinese primary schools is similar to the complex interplay that is found in non-Asian settings, but that some differences can be explained with the Chinese context in which the study was set up.

teachers’ constructivist teaching belief is indirectly related to ICT integration in the classrooms through teachers’ computer motivation, their attitudes towards the use of computers in education and their perceptions of the school policy regarding ICT.

“Teachers’ constructivist beliefs indirectly affect their classroom use of ICT through teachers’ attitudes towards computers and their perception of school ICT policy, while teachers’ computer motivation directly affects classroom use of ICT.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of a set of teacher-related factors in the Chinese context and their interplay on ICT classroom integration.
the complex interplay among teacher-related factors that influence the level of ICT integration in the Chinese classroom.
the interplay of teacher related variables and their effect on ICT integration in the Chinese context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the complex interplay among the teacher variables in the Chinese context is not very much different from the complex interplay in other countries.
the complex interplay is similar but not equal in the Chinese context.
the interplay between the teacher-related variables and the ICT integration in the Chinese classroom is complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICT integration in classroom teaching is the result of the complex interplay and interdependency of teacher-related variables, and that this interplay is partly different from the non-Asian context.
the complex interplay among teachers’ beliefs, attitudes and motivation, and their perception of ICT-related school policies, influences the extent to which they integrate ICT in their teaching.
ICT integration in the Chinese primary school context is not so much a matter of ‘how much’ teachers use computers but rather a matter of ‘what’ teachers use the computer for.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICT integration in Chinese primary classrooms is a complex phenomenon that cannot be explained by a single variable or a single theory.
teachers’ constructivist teaching philosophy and their attitudes towards ICT are important factors in the adoption and integration of ICT into their teaching.
teachers who are motivated to use computers and who perceive that their schools support the use of computers are more likely to integrate ICT in the classroom.
